title: Bug: ONIE install intermittently leaves DUT unbootable on master (kernel 6.12/Trixie) — boot hangs early
author: croos12
body:
### Is it platform specific

mellanox

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

After a successful onie-nos-install of a master (kernel 6.12.41+deb13-sonic-amd64, Debian Trixie), the DUT intermittently fails to boot into the new image. On serial console the box freezes at the GRUB hand-off and never reaches a usable kernel.

Root cause: [patches-sonic/revert-acpi-osl-use-threaded-irq-for-sci.patch](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-linux-kernel/commit/7113ba807ec0c01ffd86820637120cc968c46585), which reverts the upstream 6.12 change that made the ACPI SCI interrupt threaded, forcing it back to a hard IRQ and altering early-boot interrupt-servicing timing globally.  Removing the patch fixes the issue.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a master/master_RC image (kernel 6.12) via ONIE (onie-nos-install /tmp/sonic-<vendor>.bin).
2. Let the DUT reboot into the installed image; watch the serial console.
3. Repeat — roughly 1 in 3 boots hangs at the GRUB kernel/initrd load.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual: Boot hangs after GRUB loads the kernel/initrd

Expected: DUT boots into the installed image reliably

### Relevant log output

```shell
Booting 'SONiC-OS-master'
Loading SONiC-OS OS kernel ...
Loading SONiC-OS OS initial ramdisk ...
EFI stub: UEFI Secure Boot is enabled.
<hangs forever>
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

linkedPullRequests.title: Cherry-pick int0002 IRQF_ONESHOT removal on top of the SCI revert
linkedPullRequests.author: croos12
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

With the ACPI SCI back on a plain `IRQF_SHARED` `request_irq()`, the INT0002 virtual GPIO
driver — which shares that IRQ line — still requests it with `IRQF_ONESHOT`. The mismatched
flags make `request_irq()` fail and `int0002_vgpio` fail to probe.

The visible symptom is a boot-time hang: after a successful ONIE install the switch freezes due to the kernel boot not progressing (~30% reproduction on SN5600). Dropping `IRQF_ONESHOT` resolves it.

#### How I did it

- Added `patches-sonic/platform-x86-int0002-remove-irqf-oneshot.patch`, backporting stable
  commit `5938fb0e3285` ("platform/x86: int0002: Remove IRQF_ONESHOT from request_irq()",
  upstream `f6bc712877f2`).
- Registered the patch in `patches-sonic/series`.

#### How to verify it

1. Build and boot a master_RC image on affected x86 hardware.
2. Confirm `int0002_vgpio` probes cleanly — `dmesg | grep -i int0002` shows no
   `IRQF_SHARED`/flags-mismatch error and no `request_irq` failure.
3. Confirm the IRQ is registered and shared: `grep int0002 /proc/interrupts`.

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)
- [x] master

#### Description for the changelog

Remove IRQF_ONESHOT from INT0002 request_irq() to fix shared-IRQ flags mismatch

linkedPullRequests.title: Fully revert ACPI SCI Handler to Bookworm Behavior
linkedPullRequests.author: croos12
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Reverting `7a36b901a6eb` ("ACPI: OSL: Use a threaded interrupt handler for SCI") puts the ACPI SCI
back on a non-threaded handler requested with plain IRQF_SHARED. Three later upstream commits had
adjusted the surrounding code to suit the threaded, IRQF_ONESHOT SCI:

- `8e57de4307` dropped the interrupt disable from the ACPICA spin lock primitives.
- `655a6e7c0d` threaded the EC dedicated IRQ handler.
- `8f812373d1` added IRQF_ONESHOT to the INT0002 request.

Restore all three to their pre-`7a36b901a6eb` behavior, so the ACPI locking, the EC dedicated IRQ,
and the INT0002 flags match the SCI handler we restored.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: N/A

#### How I did it
- Re-land `revert-acpi-osl-use-threaded-irq-for-sci.patch` (#580) and
  `platform-x86-int0002-remove-irqf-oneshot.patch` (#607), which already carries the INT0002 side.
- Add `revert-acpi-osl-use-spin-locks-without-disabling-interrupts.patch` and
  `revert-acpi-ec-use-threaded-handler-for-dedicated-irq.patch`.
- Keep the four ordered as one block in `series`, matching upstream `master`, with a comment noting
  they are a dependent set.

#### How to verify it

1. Reboot repeatedly from ONIE Install, SONiC Reboot, and Power Cycling to confirm hang does not occur on kernel start

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)
- [x] master

#### Description for the changelog

Fully revert ACPI SCI Handler to Bookworm Behavior
